title: Opt-Miner: Empowering Information-Seeking Agent with Tree-Guided Data Synthesis for Optimization Modeling
one_liner: Train an optimization-modeling agent to notice missing knowledge, retrieve the needed material, and build the math model after it has grounded the problem details.
lead: Optimization-modeling tasks often mix domain facts with formal math structure. A language model may know common modeling patterns, yet still fail when a real problem depends on industry-specific rules or technical details that are not already in the model. Opt-Miner trains an agent to notice those gaps and retrieve source material first, because a grounded model is less likely to choose the wrong formulation than one that guesses from partial knowledge.

problem.h2: Why optimization modeling fails on knowledge-heavy cases
paras: Writing an optimization model is not only a matter of algebra. The agent must understand the real scenario, find the right constraints, and choose a fitting method. If the scenario depends on domain rules that are missing, the model may formalize the wrong problem.

Static pretraining is often not enough. A model can know general modeling patterns and still miss a technical regulation, an industry convention, or a special objective. In those cases, the agent must seek information actively because the missing fact changes how the optimization problem should be written.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Synthesize training problems with planted knowledge gaps and train the agent to retrieve the missing material before finishing the model.

panels.title: 1. A real problem arrives
panels.viz_args: The agent receives a scenario plus a modeling goal
panels.caption: The scenario may depend on technical facts that are not stated plainly.

panels.title: 2. The agent notices a gap
panels.viz_args: A missing rule or method blocks the model
panels.caption: The agent should not continue by guessing because the missing fact may change the whole formulation.

panels.title: 3. Retrieve supporting documents
panels.viz_args: Search the web for the missing technical detail
panels.caption: External material supplies the fact that the model lacks.

panels.title: 4. Build the formulation with that evidence
panels.caption: The new evidence changes which objective and constraints are appropriate.

panels.title: 5. Produce the final model
panels.caption: The result is stronger because the model is grounded in retrieved domain facts.

steps.b: Turn each problem into a tree
steps.text: Organize scenario details and technical methods into structured branches so that data synthesis can recombine them.
Union, transfer, and hide parts of the tree so that the training problem contains real knowledge gaps.
Reward the agent for finding missing material before finishing the formulation because correct retrieval should improve modeling quality.
Use the retrieved documents when choosing objectives, variables, and constraints.
Update the policy from relative performance across candidate solutions so that better information-seeking behavior is reinforced.

paras: The paper changes what the agent does before it writes the model. Instead of jumping directly from problem text to formal formulation, it inserts an explicit stage for gap detection and retrieval.
object.object: the agent's decision about whether to retrieve outside knowledge before modeling

hidden.name: which missing fact is blocking the correct model
paras: The key hidden quantity is the missing piece of knowledge that prevents the right formulation. The agent can sense that something is unclear, but it does not directly observe which document or concept will fix the problem until it searches.

Opt-Miner trains the agent to map from a partial scenario to that missing-knowledge decision. When the agent identifies the right gap, retrieval becomes useful because the fetched material can change the formal model in the needed place.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark hidden gaps where retrieval is most likely to change the final formulation.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is the missing fact that the agent must discover before it can write the right optimization model.
The method teaches information seeking by generating training problems where important branches of problem knowledge are deliberately obscured.

mechanism.h2: Why this works: force the agent to earn the missing knowledge
paras: An agent that is always trained on fully specified textbook problems can learn to rush into formulation. That habit breaks on real cases because many real cases omit a needed detail. Opt-Miner changes the training data so that some critical detail is missing on purpose, which makes retrieval part of the successful solution path.

The tree-guided synthesis matters because it creates structured hard cases instead of random noisy cases. By recombining scenario branches and method branches, the training set produces problems where the missing knowledge changes the formulation in a real way. The policy update then favors agents that retrieve the right material before committing to a formulation.

stages.s: Optimization scenario with a planted knowledge gap
Search for the missing technical material
Ground the formulation in that material
Reward the stronger grounded solution because retrieved facts improved the formulation
A better information-seeking modeling agent because it learns when outside facts are needed

math.h2: Prefer policies that retrieve and model well together
math.words: A compact summary is to score each candidate solution by combining retrieval quality and final modeling quality. The policy is updated toward candidates with larger combined score.
symbols: overall value of one candidate information-seeking path
how good the final optimization model is
how useful the retrieved material is for the task
weight on the retrieval part of the score

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Path A skips retrieval and writes a model with quality 5.
Its retrieval quality is 0, so with gamma = 1 its total score is 5.
Path B retrieves a domain rule and then writes a model with quality 7.
Its retrieval quality is 2, so total score is 9.
Training prefers Path B because the outside material improved the final formulation.

math.note: The paper uses a more detailed policy-optimization rule, but this score captures the point that retrieval is only valuable when it improves the final model because extra search alone is not the goal.

charts.title: Static modeling agent
charts.note: An agent that relies only on built-in knowledge misses technical details, so harder cross-domain cases remain weak.

charts.title: Opt-Miner
charts.note: The paper reports strong gains because the agent learns to retrieve the missing domain facts before finalizing the model.

items.b: Retrieval can find the wrong document.
items.html: If the agent grounds the formulation in a weak or irrelevant source, the final model can become more confidently wrong.

items.b: Synthesized gaps may differ from real gaps.
items.html: Training gaps are generated from a tree recipe, so real industrial cases may still contain messier missing knowledge than the agent saw during training.
A policy that searches too often can waste time and distract itself with extra material, even when the original problem already contained enough information.
The framework matters because it teaches the agent to treat uncertainty as a reason to seek evidence, not as a reason to guess.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a set of optimization problems where some needed domain facts are hidden outside the prompt. Compare a direct modeling agent against an Opt-Miner style agent that can search a document collection before writing the formulation. Score both on objective choice, constraint correctness, and final solver result.

The demo should show that the information-seeking agent wins on the hidden-fact cases because retrieval supplies the missing rule. Log which document was fetched and which part of the final model changed so that the mechanism stays visible.
demo.metric_eq: grounding_gain = model_score_opt_miner - model_score_direct ; retrieval_hit_rate = useful_fetches / total_fetches
demo.closing: The result should make clear that knowledge seeking can be part of optimization modeling itself.
